response.rationale: “Cemas” is an ordinary Indonesian term for feeling worried or uneasy, while Malaysian Malay commonly prefers “risau” for the same sense. The contrast is a useful usage preference, not exclusive ownership.
response.risk_rationale: Malaysian Malay also uses “cemas” in the same sense, so the national preference should not be taught as an absolute distinction.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Cemas” is also understood and used in Malaysian Malay, while “risau” is the more characteristic everyday preference there; this remains a useful contrast without implying exclusivity.
